title: Add rollout SLO evaluation + auto-decision metrics (cardinality-safe labels)
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Context: As part of the auto-rollback on SLO breach work, we need canonical, dashboardable metrics for (a) SLO evaluation outcomes and (b) the controller’s resulting decision (pause/rollback/suppress/no-op). This PR implements the runtime/controller-side metrics only (no dashboards/alerts here) and bakes in label/cardinality constraints so we don’t accidentally ship a rollout_id label and melt Prometheus. Related: ENG-4837, PRs #28411 (evaluator hook), #28458 (monitor adapter), #28463 (debounce/min sample). What’s in this PR: 1) New metrics (names + types): - rollouts_slo_eval_total (counter): increments once per evaluation tick per scope, labeled with outcome + signal. - rollouts_slo_eval_duration_seconds (histogram): evaluator loop duration (end-to-end), labeled with outcome only. - rollouts_auto_action_total (counter): increments when we take (or suppress) an action, labeled with action + reason. - rollouts_monitor_state_total (counter): monitor fetch results (ok/stale/missing/error), labeled with provider + result. - rollouts_policy_applied_total (counter): increments when we apply/resolve a policy version for a rollout scope (useful to verify config propagation), labeled with policy_source + policy_version_hash. 2) Canonical label set (bounded) applied consistently across metrics: - service: rollout controller target service (e.g. "gateway", "embeddings") - route: normalized route name (bounded; uses route template, not full path) - model: model family (e.g. "llama-3.1") - model_version: pinned serving version (bounded per environment; validated by controller) - region: cloud region (bounded) - customer_tier: self_serve|dedicated|private - signal: latency_p95|latency_p99|error_rate|saturation (only on eval counters) - outcome: ok|breach_fast|breach_slow|insufficient_samples|monitor_stale|monitor_missing|monitor_error|suppressed_known_incident - action: none|pause|rollback|shift_to_baseline|suppressed (only on auto_action counter) - reason: fast_burn|slow_burn|stale_data|missing_monitor|min_samples|holdoff_active|manual_suppress|incident_override|policy_guardrail (only on auto_action counter) 3) Explicit cardinality guardrails: - DO NOT include rollout_id, org_id, project_id, or raw model_id in metric labels. This PR adds a small helper that rejects disallowed label keys at construction time (unit-tested). - rollouts_policy_applied_total uses policy_version_hash (8-char prefix of sha256) instead of full policy version string to avoid label explosions. - route label uses a precomputed route template from the router config (e.g. "/v1/chat/completions") rather than user-provided paths. 4) Examples + docs in-code for dashboards/queries: Added a doc block with PromQL snippets for the observability-pack PR to copy/paste: - Auto actions by service/region over 1h: sum by (service, region, action) (increase(rollouts_auto_action_total[1h])) - Missing/stale monitors rate: sum by (service, region, result) (increase(rollouts_monitor_state_total{result=~"missing|stale"}[15m])) - Breach outcomes by signal: sum by (signal, outcome) (increase(rollouts_slo_eval_total{outcome=~"breach_.*"}[30m])) - Evaluator overhead p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(rollouts_slo_eval_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) Notes/behavioral details: - rollouts_slo_eval_total is emitted after the evaluator computes a terminal outcome for that tick (including staleness/missing/sample gating), so we can distinguish “no breach” from “no data”. - rollouts_auto_action_total increments only when the controller writes a decision (including suppressed decisions) to the audit stream; it should correlate 1:1 with audit events once #28435 is live. - We intentionally keep “reason” and “outcome” separate: outcome describes the SLO evaluation; reason describes why we took (or didn’t take) an action. Tests: - Unit tests for label allow/deny list, route normalization, policy hash shaping, and “no rollout_id in labels” regression. - Golden test verifying metric names/types and label sets. Rollout/compatibility: - No breaking change for existing metrics. - Metrics are behind the existing feature flag rollouts.slo_evaluator.enabled for now; when disabled, no new series should be emitted. - Follow-up: observability-pack PR will add dashboards + alert rules once naming is locked. Checklist: - [x] Metrics names reviewed against observability standards draft - [x] Cardinality review (no rollout_id/org_id) - [x] Added unit tests - [x] Verified metrics in staging via /metrics and local prom scrape
commits: rollouts: normalize route label to template name
policy: hash policy version string for bounded label
tests: label guardrails + golden metric registry test
docs: add PromQL examples for dashboards
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Please confirm we are not introducing rollout_id or anything user-scoped as a label. Also, can we keep label keys aligned with the draft rollouts/SLO naming standard (service/route/model/model_version/region/tier)?

Caleb Johnson (author): Confirmed: no rollout_id/org_id/project_id labels; I added a denylist enforced in code + tests. Label keys match the standard: service, route (template), model, model_version, region, customer_tier. Signal/outcome/action/reason are bounded enums.

Aisha Bello (review): For dashboards, I’d like an easy way to see “monitor missing/stale” vs “insufficient samples” so oncall knows whether to blame telemetry vs real regression. Can outcome include those as terminal states?

Caleb Johnson (author): Yep — outcome includes monitor_missing, monitor_stale, monitor_error, insufficient_samples. Also added rollouts_monitor_state_total with provider+result so we can alert on missing/stale separately from eval outcomes.
Jada Williams (review): rollouts_policy_applied_total: do we really need policy_version as a label? That can blow up if customers roll policies often.

Caleb Johnson (author): Agree. I switched to policy_version_hash (8 chars) and kept policy_source. Also gated emission behind the same evaluator feature flag so we don’t emit for every rollout in prod until we’re ready.

Logan Wright (review): Histogram buckets: evaluator duration doesn’t need super fine granularity. Can we use the standard latency buckets from telemetry lib and keep outcome as the only label? We don’t want signal/action on histograms.
Caleb Johnson (author): Done — duration histogram uses standard buckets and only labels by outcome (bounded). No signal/action labels on histograms.
Allison Grant (final): +1 with the guardrails. Please add a short comment near the metric definitions explaining why rollout_id is forbidden and where to find it (audit logs).
Caleb Johnson (author): Added comment in metrics_registry.go: rollout_id is in audit events/traces, not metrics. Pushed final commit.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved. PromQL examples are helpful; I’ll reference them in the observability-pack dashboard PR.
release_notes: Internal: rollout controller exports new metrics for SLO eval outcomes and auto actions (cardinality-safe labels); to be consumed by upcoming dashboards/alerts.
